extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians in arithmetic geometry and readers of Mochizuki's inter-universal Teichmüller theory
extracted.subtask_description: Exposition and technical construction steps in Mochizuki-style inter-universal Teichmüller theory focused on theta-related varieties, etale theta functions, and the group-theoretic reconstruction machinery needed for the cyclotomic rigidity/isomorphism. Targets specialists needing the precise algebraic/analytic constructions used in IUT.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use tempered fundamental groups
rubrics_metrics.description: In inter-universal Teichmüller theory, we need to use tempered fundamental groups, because the theory of the étale theta function (cf. Section 7) plays a crucial role.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tempered fundamental groups are required for the étale-theta-function constructions and related analytic structures; note tempered fundamental groups are available only over non-Archimedean local fields, so their use constrains which local fields one works over.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use profinite fundamental groups
rubrics_metrics.description: We also need to use profinite fundamental groups, because we need hyperbolic orbicurve over a number field for the purpose of putting "labels" for each places in a consistent manner (cf. Proposition 10.19 and Proposition 10.33).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Profinite (i.e., pro-finite) fundamental groups are used to handle global arithmetic labeling across places (orbicurves over number fields). The interplay between profinite and tempered structures is essential: each has a distinct role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Profinite Conjugates vs. Tempered Conjugates (Theorem 6.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: The pro-finite conjugacy indeterminacy is reduced to the harmless tempered conjugacy indeterminacy (Theorem 6.11).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One should use Theorem 6.11 (and Lemma 11.9) to control conjugacy indeterminacy: reconstructible objects that are only well-defined up to profinite conjugacy can be made meaningful by passing to tempered conjugacy, which the author treats as harmless for the intended reconstructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group-theoretic reconstruction of inertia and decomposition groups of cusps
rubrics_metrics.description: Let X be a smooth hyperbolic log-curve over K. Then we can group-theoretically reconstruct the inertia subgroups and the decomposition groups of cusps in temp(X) (Corollary 6.12).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reconstruction uses Lemma 6.2 (with Remark 6.2.1), Corollary 2.9, Remark 2.9.2, and Theorem 6.11; pro-finite completions and residual finiteness arguments (Proposition C.5) are invoked. Note reconstructions in pro-finite completions have profinite-conjugacy indeterminacy, which is reduced to tempered-conjugacy indeterminacy by Theorem 6.11.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconstruct dual semi-graph of the special fiber from group data
rubrics_metrics.description: By combining Corollary 6.12 with Proposition 6.6, we can group-theoretically reconstruct the dual semi-graph of the special fibre (Remark 6.12.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reconstruction of the dual semi-graph is a prerequisite for later constructions (e.g., positive rational structure on H^2); prior algorithms (e.g., profGC) are referenced for analogous reconstructions from profinite fundamental groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construct positive rational structure on H^2 and obtain cyclotomic rigidity via LCFT
rubrics_metrics.description: From the reconstructed dual semi-graph one can reconstruct (1) a positive rational structure on H^2((1)X; Z^(GK))_ and (2) hence a cyclotomic rigidity isomorphism ("Cyc. Rig. via Pos. Rat. Str.") Z^(GK) → Z^((5)X) (Remark 6.12.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The construction uses finite étale coverings to arrange that irreducible components of special fiber have genus ≥ 2 and that the 'new parts' of Jacobians are ordinary; then Raynaud's theorem, polarisation via the theta divisor, non-degenerate cup product restrictions, and the Riemann hypothesis for abelian varieties over finite fields yield unique GK-splittings producing a positive Q-structure on H^2. These steps are technical and require passing to finite covers and unramified extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use value group portion (O1 not O2) in cyclotomic rigidity construction
rubrics_metrics.description: It is important to use the value group portion (i.e., use O1, not O2) in the construction of the surjection H^1(GK; Z^(GK)) → Hom(H^1(GK; Z); Z) and hence in the construction of the cyclotomic rigidity via positive rational structure and LCFT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The content of reconstruction algorithms (not just their existence) matters; whether the algorithm uses the value-group portion is crucial for constructions in the final multiradial algorithm in IUT. See Remarks 9.6.2, 11.4.1, Proposition 11.5, Remark 11.11.1 for further dependence on this choice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduce étale theta functions and mono-theta environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 7 introduces the theory of the étale theta functions and the notion of mono-theta environment, described as probably the most important ingredient of IUT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 7.1 builds theta-related varieties; Section 7.4 defines the mono-theta environment. These notions are central to later constructions and require the prior group-theoretic reconstructions and the theta quotient constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define theta-related quotients and exact sequences (theta quotient, theta-ell, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a stable curve X of type (1;1) with singular geometrically irreducible special fibre and smooth Raynaud generic fibre, define various quotients like (1)X, (1)(2)X, the theta quotient (1)X := (1)X/[(1)X,[(1)X,(1)X]] and associated exact sequences and images ((1)temp X)(2), ((1)temp X)ell, etc. (Section 7.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These group quotients and exact sequences set up the algebraic framework for the theta constructions; keep track of which kernels (e.g., Z corresponding to universal graph-covering) are being quotiented and the resulting central extensions (bZ(1), bZ).

rubrics_metrics.name: Construct infinite étale covering Y (Gal(Y/X)=Z) and line bundles LN with degree 1 on components
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct Y as the infinite étale covering corresponding to kernel ((1)temp X) → Z; Y is an infinite chain of projective lines joined at nodes, components labelled by Z; for YN (finite-level coverings) define line bundles LN with degree 1 on each irreducible component and identify Pic(YN) ≅ Z^Z (Section 7.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This geometric picture (infinite chains, labelling by Z, Picard identification) is used to define Cartier divisors, theta trivialisations, and to construct the theta functions. The degrees on components determine isomorphism classes of line bundles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of N-th roots s_N and compatible faithful actions on LN (Lemma 7.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) The section s1|YN (whose zero locus is the cusps) has an N-th root sN over ZN. (2) There is a unique action of temp_pi1 on LN (over OKN) compatible with sN; furthermore this action factors through (temp_pi1)ZN and is faithful (Lemma 7.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proof uses theta-group/Heisenberg-group structure, finite Galois coverings ZN, tautological torsors RN, and comparison of coverings; the N-th root is unique up to OKN-multiples and the temp_pi1-action is determined by compatibility with the section and faithfulness follows from the zeroes of s1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define the étale theta cohomology class via differences of compatible actions (Definition 7.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: By comparing two compatible systems of actions of (temp_pi1) on the compatible family of (YN, LN, sN) (one coming from Lemma 7.1 actions and another from a chosen system of trivializations), take the difference to obtain a cohomology class in H^1((temp_pi1)_{(127)Y}; (1)(2)) (Definition 7.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The resulting cohomology class (the étale theta class) is well-defined up to OK^×-multiples; it arises from an inverse limit over N and its restriction to finite levels corresponds to the tautological isomorphisms. The class can be related to Galois cohomology via the Kummer map.

rubrics_metrics.name: Canonical integral/discrete/tame/f1g-structures for cuspidal decomposition groups and compatibility of sections (Definition 7.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define the canonical integral structure of a cuspidal decomposition group Dy as the reduction of the Sect(Dy→GL) torsor to the canonical O_L^×-torsor given by tangential basepoint constructions; define canonical discrete and tame integral structures and f1g- or (Z_l)^{2l}-structures. A section is said to be compatible with a given structure if it comes from the corresponding torsor (Definition 7.3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives a rigidity/control on which splittings (sections) are admissible for arithmetic/étale theta constructions, reducing the pro-finite torsor structure to integral or tame sub-torsors using the canonical lattice of cotangent directions at cusps. Important when relating local tangential sections to global cohomology classes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construct theta function on double cover and meromorphic extension (Lemma 7.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define an explicit theta-like function (127)(2)( (127)U ) as an infinite sum formula on the double cover (127)U which extends uniquely to a meromorphic function on (127)Y, mirroring classical complex theta functions (Lemma 7.4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One works on the double covering because the theta function requires a square root coordinate; the explicit q-expansion and the analogy with classical complex theta functions guide the arithmetic-analytic properties needed for IUT.
